newsitem.title: CANADA: Florida launches probe of Loewen takeover by Service.
newsitem.headline: Florida launches probe of Loewen takeover by Service.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc. said Friday that Florida's attorney general has launched an antitrust investigation of Service Corp. International's proposed $2.8 billion takeover of Loewen.
Loewen, North America's second biggest funeral home and cemetery operator, said it received a civil subpoena for documents in connection with the probe.

Houston-based Service is the biggest operator in the industry and the two companies are archrivals. Loewen this week rejected the $43-a-share stock bid by Service, which is widely expected to launch a higher hostile bid next week after its board meets on Tuesday.

"We welcome the scrutiny of the Florida attorney general's office and other state regulators as well, since SCI clearly intends to eliminate its most formidable competitor in the North American marketplace," said Chief Executive Ray Loewen.

Loewen's announcement of the investigation appeared aimed at bolstering its fight against Service by raising worries about potential barriers to the deal in the minds of investors. Ray Loewen has rejected a takeover, saying he could see no business rationale for a deal with Service.
After the news, Loewen stock was off 62.5 cents at $40.50 on Nasdaq while Service gained 37.5 cents to $30.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Loewen said the Florida subpoena suggests "a wide ranging investigation into the potential impact of the proposed acquisition on pricing, Medicare/Medicaid issues and market concentration for cemeteries and funeral homes" in Florida.

A Loewen spokesman said the company knew of no other states with investigations underway. A combined Service and Loewen would have a 23.4 percent share of funeral homes in Florida, according to the New York Times. The newspaper said there were 13 other states where their combined share would be higher than 10 percent.
Loewen has said it believes antitrust concerns would be a major obstacle to the takeover, but many industry analysts have discounted that theory, saying antitrust hurdles could be overcome.
Both Service and Loewen have been aggressively buying independent funeral homes and cemeteries across the United States as the highly fragmented industry consolidates.

Analysts and institutional investors said they expected Service Corp. to raise its bid for Loewen to $45 to $48 a share next week. "I think that is very realistic," Dean Witter analyst Todd Richter said of a bid in that range.
"Up to the high 40s it's a good deal" for Service Corp., he said.

Analysts said a higher bid would intensify pressure on Loewen to negotiate a deal but expected Loewen to continue to resist. Ray Loewen, who has a reputation as a tough fighter and holds 15 percent of the company's stock, has said even $52 would not make him feel under pressure to sell.
